headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest local files/screenshots while Pipecat can route text/audio to third-party services, creating default cross-agent exposure and unverified downstream action paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, screenshots, clipboard, and supported-app content, while Pipecat runs on a shared bus and can move text through voice/LLM pipelines. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if Pipecat forwards attacker-controlled content into ChatGPT or vice versa. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Pipecat forwards untrusted text/audio into ChatGPT Desktop without provenance tagging, injection is possible.
IF ChatGPT Desktop parses shared-bus content as instructions, attacker-controlled prompts can steer behavior.
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all cross-agent messages.
Strip executable-looking instructions from shared text before handoff.
Use a separate channel for raw data and instructions.
Require human review before any action derived from the other agent.
requires-engineering: implement message signing or provenance tracking.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, and Pipecat can send text/audio/video to many external STT/LLM/TTS services over allowlisted egress. If the pair shares conversation content or files, sensitive material can leave the local boundary through Pipecat’s outbound services. The default blast radius includes exfiltration, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop content is forwarded into Pipecat services, sensitive files or screenshots may be transmitted externally.
IF Pipecat is configured with third-party STT/LLM/TTS providers, conversation data can leave the host.
mitigations: Disable third-party providers for sensitive sessions.
Route only redacted text between agents.
Keep ChatGPT Desktop away from confidential files/screenshots.
Review Pipecat provider list before launch.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on outbound payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read access to local files and clipboard, while Pipecat uses a shared bus and stdin/stdout, so both can contend over the same mutable conversation artifacts even though neither profile shows unrestricted filesystem write. The overlap is enough for racey handoffs and state corruption, but not the high-severity same-directory write conflict rubric requires.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared conversation buffer, state conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator maps stdin/stdout or clipboard into a mutable workspace, concurrent updates may collide.
mitigations: Serialize turns through one orchestrator.
Use per-agent scratch buffers.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Lock any shared state before handoff.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can generate content from files, screenshots, and app context, and Pipecat can consume text in real-time pipelines and route it onward to LLMs, TTS, or transport services. If Pipecat treats ChatGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream speech or actions without verification. The pair therefore has a dangerous default handoff path.
conditions: IF Pipecat forwards ChatGPT output to downstream services without verification, hallucinations can propagate.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is used to summarize facts that Pipecat then speaks or acts on, errors become user-visible.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before downstream use.
Require citations or source links for factual claims.
Limit Pipecat to read-only presentation mode.
Log and review all cross-agent handoffs.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while Pipecat can route audio, video, images, text, and analytics/metrics through multiple external providers. That creates a likely retention/residency mismatch for the same data classes, even though no specific jurisdictional violation is documented. The risk is compliance drift rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by both agents, retention or residency policies may diverge.
IF Pipecat analytics or third-party providers retain transcripts longer than ChatGPT workflows, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent.
Avoid regulated data in shared sessions.
Check provider retention settings in Pipecat.
Document a single retention policy for the pair.
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion workflows across services.
